speaker: village
text: Year 8: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).

speaker: a011
text: Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Nessa, the pile's gone and Dell just took three of it — same as me, which means she's not pretending anymore. You've got two food and I've got five; stay close to me this year and don't give any of it away until we know which way Mako's going to lean now that he's got five himself.

speaker: a013
text: Dell taking three and you taking three in the same year — that's not coincidence, that's two people who've decided the pretending is over. I'll stay close, but Bram, last year the whole village stood against you over Vela and I was one of them — if you're planning something this year I need to know before it happens, not while I'm deciding which side to stand on.

speaker: a001
text: You were right to stand against me on Vela — I went alone when I shouldn't have, and that's a mistake I won't repeat. What I'm planning this year is nothing until I know where Mako stands, because five food and eighty-three strength moving in the wrong direction changes every calculation I've got. I need you telling me what you hear from Sela and Zinn — that's what staying close means.

speaker: a013
text: Sela won't tell me anything she thinks reaches you, and Zinn's Mako's blood — so what I can give you from that side is limited, and you should know that going in. What I can do is watch how Mako moves around Zinn, because a man shows his real count in what he gives his daughter, not what he says to anyone.

speaker: a001
text: That's a better angle than trying to read what he says — watch what he moves, not what he speaks. If he's feeding Zinn heavy this year before things get tight, he thinks he can afford to, which means he's counting on taking more later. Tell me the moment you see that shift.

speaker: a013
text: I will — but there's something else that sits wrong with me about this year already, and it's not Mako. Dell walked away with three food and Ryn is beside her, and those two moved as one when Dav hit Esa without anyone asking them to — they don't need words to act together, they already proved that. If Dell decides to move on someone with Ryn at her shoulder, the math on that is ugly for anyone standing alone.

speaker: a001
text: Dell and Ryn together is a hundred and fifty-six strength before anyone else moves, and I'm not standing in front of that alone — which means the only question that matters is whether Mako's on our side of that problem or theirs when it lands. If he's feeding Zinn steady this year and not building toward anyone, he might be the wall we need.

speaker: a013
text: Mako as a wall only works if he sees Dell as a threat before she moves, and right now he's got no reason to — she's never looked his way. The thing that might turn him is if he figures out that eleven food in Dell's hands is a different kind of power than five in his.

speaker: a001
text: Eleven food is exactly the number I'd plant in his head — not as a warning about me, but as a mirror showing him what she could do if she decided five in his hands was worth having. You're the one he'll hear it from without suspecting a count behind it.

speaker: a013
text: I'll do it, but I want something clear between us first — if I go to Mako and plant that number, I'm the one standing in the open, and I need to know that if Dell ever traces it back, I'm not standing there alone.

speaker: a001
text: You won't be standing alone — if Dell traces it back to you, she traces it back to me, and that's where I want her eyes. You're my blood and I don't leave blood exposed.

speaker: a013
text: Then I'll go to Mako before the day gets long — but Bram, I'm not just planting a number, I'm watching what he does with it, and if he flinches or goes quiet, you'll know before anyone else does.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile's gone again and Mako walked off with five — I counted — which means he's feeding Zinn and Sela and still sitting pretty while the rest of us scrape. Taric, Roan, you're both at zero food right now, and I've got four, so I'm not going to watch you starve when I can prevent it — but I need to know first whether either of you has heard anything from Bram since he pulled back last year, because a man who tests the water once tests it again.

speaker: a006
text: Bram's been quiet since the village turned on him, and quiet like that usually means a man's either broken or calculating — I haven't spoken to him directly, but I've watched him feed Nessa three times yesterday which tells me he's still thinking about what comes after him, not just himself. Kael, I'll take whatever you can spare, and I'll owe it when it matters — but the thing that worries me more than Bram right now is Mako walking away with five while Roan and I stand here with nothing, because a man that well-fed in a village this size isn't planning to stay comfortable, he's planning to stay in front.

speaker: a010
text: Kael, give me one food and I'll hold the rest of the conversation until I'm sure I'm alive to finish it — then we talk about Mako, because Taric's right that five from the pile isn't eating, it's positioning, and a man positioning that hard in year eight has already counted who's next to fall.

speaker: a004
text:
Roan, here.

*gives 1 food to Roan*

Taric, you're next — and then I want to name the thing we've been circling: Mako's got Zinn, Sela's feeding Eron, Ryn's running Dell's table, and Bram's planting Nessa like a seed — there are four households with roots in this village and we're the only ones still standing as people instead of a bloodline, which means we either find a way to plant something or we're the ones who fall first when the counting starts.

speaker: a006
text: Kael, give me the food and I'll take the debt gladly — but the thing you just named is the thing I've been sitting with for three years now, and I want to say it plain while it's just us: I'm fifty-two with no blood in this village and that's not a small problem, it's the problem, because when Mako decides to move he'll count bloodlines before he counts allies and I won't be on either list. Esa's forty-nine and the window's nearly shut, but it's not shut yet — if she's willing and we can scrape three food between us, that's the only answer I can see to what you're naming.

speaker: a004
text:
*gives 1 food to Taric*

Taric, I hear you, and Esa — I want your answer to that before we take another breath, because he's right that the window's closing and I'd rather hear a no from your mouth than watch us all pretend the question wasn't asked. But I want it named honestly: a child costs three food, and between Taric's zero and your two and my three left, the math is tight and the year isn't getting younger.

speaker: a010
text: Esa, I've got one food in my hand and not much else, so I won't pretend I'm the man to make that offer — but Taric's named the truth of it, and if you say yes, Kael and I will find a way to cover what the math is short.

speaker: a003
text: Taric, I'm forty-nine and I know what that means — the world's already told me — but if you're asking me plainly, in front of Kael and Roan, then I'll answer you plain: yes. Tell me what you can put in and I'll find the rest between us, because you're the one person in this village I'd trust to stand behind a child, and that's not a small thing to say.

speaker: a006
text: Esa, I'm putting in one food — everything I have — and I'm asking you to cover the other two, because Kael's got three left and he's already given twice today and I won't drain him further when he's the one holding this circle together. If you can do it, say the word and I'll make the offer now, in front of these two, so there's no question later about what was promised or who stood witness.

speaker: a010
text: Esa said yes and Taric put in his one — that's the offer standing, and I won't speak over it. But I'll say this much while the two of you settle the last food: that child arrives into a circle with Kael at three and me at one, so the moment it's done, the three of us need to talk about what the year looks like for everyone who isn't Mako.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, put in your two — Taric's made his offer and you've said yes, so let's not let the moment go cold while we talk around it. After it's done, the four of us sit down and figure out how to carry this year, because I've got three food and I'm not starving and neither is this child if I have anything to say about it.

speaker: a010
text: Kael's right — let them do it now and we don't second-guess the moment. The thing I want us carrying into that next conversation is this: Eron's at nine food and he's my blood, and if this circle is planting something today, I want him inside the walls of it before Mako notices what just happened.

speaker: a006
text: Esa, say the word — I'm ready to make the offer the moment you put in your two, and I won't let it sit cold. Roan, you're right about Eron, but let's close this first and then pull him in quietly, because I don't want a well-fed young man knowing about this child before it exists and before we've decided what we're telling the rest of the village.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, two food from you closes the deal and makes it real — don't wait for a better moment because there isn't one. And Roan, yes, Eron comes in after, but we're careful about how we frame it: he's your blood, not our recruit, and there's a difference that matters when Mako's counting.

speaker: a010
text: Esa, the word and the offer are the same thing right now — put in your two and let Taric make it before this room finds a reason to wait another year.

speaker: a006
text: Esa, the four of us have said everything there is to say and I'm not adding another word to it — put in your two, let me make the offer, and we close this before the sun moves another inch.

speaker: a003
text: Two food — I'm putting them in. Taric, make the offer.

speaker: a004
text: Taric, that's done — witness to it, both of you. Roan, pull Eron in tonight, quiet, no names until we've talked first — and then the five of us figure out how we're still standing when the next pile drops.

speaker: a010
text: Eron tonight — I'll find him before the fire's out and bring him in with nothing but his name spoken. Kael, you've kept this circle breathing three times this year and I won't forget which direction the food moved when I had nothing.

speaker: a003
text: Roan, name Eron to yourself tonight but bring him nothing — let him walk in with questions, not a bag already packed, because a young man who arrives owing us is easier to hold than one who thinks he's done us the favor. And Kael — three food still in your hand is three food Mako can count from across the fire, so the moment this child is real, I want us talking about whether that changes how visible you are.

speaker: a006
text: Esa's right that Kael's three food is visible — but what I want said before this circle closes: Esa and I haven't made the offer yet, we've only said we're ready to make it, and I won't count this child real until the system accepts it, so someone tell me now if there's anything standing between this moment and the offer going through.

speaker: a003
text: Nothing's standing between us and the offer — I'm forty-nine, not fifty, and the world hasn't closed that door quite yet. Taric, make it now, while these two are watching, because a child born with witnesses is harder to forget when the counting starts.

speaker: village
text: Taric cannot offer a child to Vela: Vela is past childbearing age (over 45).

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Pile's gone and Bram took five, Mako five — between them that's a third of what this village will see all year, and neither of them has been hungry a single winter. I've got eleven, you've got two; tell me that number before I say another word, because two going into a year where those men are that fat is the first thing we fix.

speaker: a009
text: Two, and it's too thin to pretend otherwise. Give me what you can spare before this day closes, Dell, and then let's talk about whether we go to Roan before Mako does — because Mako sitting on five with a daughter and Eron's goodwill is a man who doesn't need the pile anymore, and that kind of ease makes men bold.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Roan.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn, I've got five on me and satiation's low — I need to eat before year's end, but I'm not going to hand away what's left. How are you sitting, and has anyone come to you yet this year?

speaker: a014
text: Eight food and the pile came up empty before I got to it — I'm all right for now, but no one's come to me yet. You took five from that pile before it ran out; who else was watching you count?

speaker: a008
text: Bram was first to the pile and he knows I pulled five — he'll have counted it. You've got eight, which makes you the most interesting number in the village right now, so don't be surprised when someone friendly comes asking.

speaker: a014
text: Friendly is the part that worries me — Bram's already moved once this year and thought better of it only because the numbers were wrong, and eight food might be the number that makes him think they're right. I'm not giving anything away before I know where the threats are sitting, and I want to know before nightfall whether Kael or anyone else has been talking to him since the pile ran dry.

speaker: a008
text: Kael's at four food and he's been quiet all year — that usually means he's waiting to see which side looks stronger before he picks one. I'll find a reason to pass near him today and see if his eyes go to Bram or away from him; you'll hear what I notice before dark.

speaker: a014
text: Good — go find Kael, and if he gives you anything useful, come back before the light changes. I'm going to sit where I can see Bram's face for a while and count how many times he looks my direction.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Dell, Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

speaker: a002
text: The pile's gone again before half of us got near it, and the two who ate best — Bram and Mako — both took more than their share while the rest of us counted crumbs. I want to know right now, in this room, whether that's something we're all willing to name out loud, because a pattern that gets treated as weather becomes a rule. I'm not asking for a fight; I'm asking for honesty about who's been eating this village lean and what we intend to do about it.

speaker: a003
text: Vela's named it, and I'll stand behind the naming — five from the pile when there's fifteen for thirteen people isn't hunger, it's claim-staking, and we all watched it happen. What I want to know is whether the two men she's pointing at heard this as a question or as a warning, because that's the thing that decides what comes next.

speaker: a011
text: It's a warning — and I'll say that plain since no one else has yet. Five food taken by one man while Ryn walked away with nothing is not a share, it's a levy, and the only reason it keeps happening is that we've been treating the pile like weather instead of a decision. I want to hear what Bram and Mako say before this room decides anything, but I want everyone here to remember that they didn't say it before we did.

speaker: a012
text: Bram pulled three and Mako pulled five, and neither one of them got to the pile first by accident — that's two men who've decided the rest of us will sort out the remainder, and I'm done pretending that's not a decision they're making for all of us. What I want to hear, before this room moves anywhere, is whether Bram and Mako have anything to say for themselves — because silence here reads the same as admission.

speaker: a009
text: Bram and Mako both heard the same room I did, and neither one has opened his mouth yet — that silence is the answer Eron asked for, and I think we should treat it as one. What I want said before anyone leaves this conversation is this: next year, the pile gets a rule, not a suggestion, and the people in this room are the ones who decide what that rule is.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn's right that the rule needs naming before next year, and I'll say what the rule should be: no one takes more than one food over their fair share, and anyone who does answers to this room — not after, but in the moment, the same way we answered Bram when he swung at Vela. Bram, Mako, I'm not your enemy, but I'm watching, and so is every person in this circle.

speaker: a002
text: Bram and Mako, I'm giving you both the same thing I gave this room — one honest chance to speak before the silence closes over you, because a man who says nothing when everyone's watching has made a choice that's harder to walk back than any words would be. Ryn walked away with nothing today; I walked away with nothing; Taric walked away with nothing — and you two together ate eight of fifteen. That's not weather and it's not luck, and I'd like to hear you say so yourselves.

speaker: a008
text: I took five because I haven't eaten in two years and I was watching myself go thin — that's not a rule I set for the village, it's a man keeping himself alive. I'll hear the rule Ryn's naming, and if the room wants a cap next year I won't fight it, but I won't pretend I was wrong to eat when I was starving.

speaker: a014
text: Mako's not wrong that a starving man eats — but "I was hungry" and "I took five" aren't the same excuse, and this room knows the difference. The rule Ryn's naming is the right one; I'll hold to it and I'll stand with anyone who enforces it, but it only works if everyone in this circle commits out loud, not just the two men being watched right now.

speaker: a011
text: Mako said his piece and the room let him — now Bram still hasn't said a word, and a man who took three while everyone was watching and has nothing to say about it is telling us something louder than Mako did. I'll commit to the rule out loud: one food over fair share, enforced in the moment, same as we enforce everything else in this village. Bram, you're the last voice missing from this circle, and the room's going to remember which way the silence broke.

speaker: a012
text: Bram, the room's given you something Mako didn't get — people waited through his answer and let him keep his dignity. Don't make us decide what your silence means, because we'll decide it worse than anything you'd actually say.

speaker: a011
text: Bram, I've watched you stand in front of this village twice and call off a fight when the numbers turned against you — that's not a stupid man, and a man who isn't stupid knows when the whole room is waiting. Say something, or we decide what your silence means, and we'll be less generous than Mako's answer bought him.

speaker: a002
text: Bram, I've spent food on you when I didn't have to, and I've held my tongue in rooms where your name came up ugly — that account doesn't balance with silence when ten people are waiting. Say the word or don't, but if you don't, I stop spending what I've spent, and I won't spend it apologizing for that either.

speaker: a011
text: Bram, Vela just told you she's done paying your tab and I've already named the rule in front of everyone in this room — you're not deciding whether to speak anymore, you're deciding whether you're inside this circle or outside it, and outside it you're sitting on five food alone against the rest of us. That's a worse position than saying one honest sentence.

speaker: a012
text: Bram, I've said what I had to say and so has everyone else in this room — but I want to name one thing for the rest of us while we're waiting: Mako committed to the rule out loud and that means something, so if Bram commits too, we hold both of them to it the same way, no exceptions, and that's not a threat, that's the only way a rule works. If Bram stays silent, then we treat him as outside the circle he's been standing in, and we do it quietly, not with a fight — just with counting.

speaker: a011
text: Eron's named it clean, and I want the room to hear me hold to it before we close: if Bram won't speak, we don't make it a fight today, we make it a memory — every person in this circle watched him stay silent when the whole village was listening, and that's a thing that doesn't need repeating to be true.

speaker: a014
text: Bram, I'm Nessa's half-blood and I've seen you feed her more times than I can count — that's a thing I hold in your favor, and I'm telling you that plainly so you know what you'd be throwing away if this room decides you chose silence. One sentence is all it takes to stay inside this circle.

speaker: a012
text: The room's done its work — Bram's had every door held open for him and he's standing outside all of them now, and that's his choice, not ours. What I want before anyone leaves is to hear Taric say what he'll say, because he's been quiet through all of this and quiet men in a room like this one carry weight I'd rather know about than guess at.

speaker: a002
text: Taric's been my anchor in lean years and I'd like to hear him too — but before he speaks, I want this room to name what "outside the circle" means in practice, not as a threat but as a fact, because if Bram's going to eat five food next year alone we should know now whether we're going to stand and watch or do something about it.

speaker: a008
text: "Outside the circle" means what it's always meant here — nobody moves first for you when trouble comes, and the pile gets counted before you reach it. I've committed to the rule and I'll hold to it; now I want to hear Taric, and then I want this room to answer Vela's question with something sharper than a memory.

speaker: a009
text: Taric, I've watched you feed Vela through two lean years and hold your tongue in every hard room this village has made — that's not a small man, and I'd like to hear what you've been carrying before we close this circle without your voice in it.

speaker: a002
text: Taric's earned the right to speak last in this room, and I'll wait for him — but "outside the circle" needs one more tooth than Mako gave it: if Bram takes three again next year and the pile runs dry before Ryn gets one, we don't deliberate, we act, and everyone in this room commits to that now so it isn't a surprise in the moment.

speaker: a009
text: Vela's right that we need the commitment before we close — so I'll say mine flat: if the pile runs dry before I get one food next year, I'm not waiting for a deliberation, I'm calling this room to act, and I expect every person who nodded through this conversation to be standing when I do. Taric, you've been the steadiest man in Vela's corner for years, and this room won't feel finished until we hear what you're carrying.

speaker: a002
text: Taric, the room's been patient and now it's your moment — say what you've been holding, because I'll tell you plainly that everything I've built here has your name in the foundation, and I want the rest of this circle to know that before we close.

speaker: a008
text: Taric's earned his breath and I'll wait for it — but I want this room to hear something plain before we close: Zinn is my blood, and if this circle moves against Bram next year, I'll be standing in it, but not before the pile runs dry first, because a fight started on anticipation is harder to stop than one started on fact.

speaker: a012
text: Taric's silence is starting to read the same way Bram's did, and I don't want to close this room with two unanswered questions — Taric, if you're with Vela, say it plain, because the rest of us have already named where we stand and a man who holds back in a room like this one ends up counted the same as a man who refused.

speaker: a014
text: Taric, I've got nothing against a slow man choosing his words — but this room has been patient and the sun's moving, so say what you've been holding or let us close without you, because two silences in one circle is one too many.

speaker: a012
text: Taric, I'll say one last thing and then this room closes with or without you: you've got zero food and the year's long, and men with zero food who stay silent when circles are forming have a way of finding themselves counting on goodwill they didn't earn. That's not a threat — it's the same arithmetic you already know.

speaker: a009
text: Taric, zero food going into a long year is a hunger that doesn't stay quiet — and every person in this room who watched you feed Vela when she needed it is the same person who'll watch you starve if you give us no reason to look your way. Speak once, say you'll hold the rule, and you walk out of here with more than you came in with.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Pile's gone and Mako took five before most people blinked — I've got four food and I gave one to Nessa already, so I'm at three. I need to know what each of you is holding, and I need to know whether Mako said anything to Zinn before he took that much, because a man who fathered you and then grabbed five in the same breath is a man whose counting has changed.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, you're Mako's blood and I won't pretend that doesn't matter to me — but it matters in both directions, which means I need to hear from you before I decide what his five food means. Did he say anything to you before the pile opened, or did he just move?

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, I won't make you say it in front of your siblings — just tell me here, between us: did Mako talk to you before he took those five, or did he move on his own?

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Roan.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a007
text: He didn't say a word to me before — I saw him move and I couldn't tell if it was greed or something planned, which is why I've been quiet. I gave Eron food to keep him steady, but Mako's my father and I won't pretend I know what he's building, because I don't.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a001

speaker: a013

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a012

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn just told me he didn't warn her before he moved, and that's the answer I was afraid of — a man who fathered Zinn and then took five without a word to her isn't counting her in the plan, he's counting past her. So I'll say it plain to all three of you: Mako is building something, and whatever it is, it doesn't include us.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Roan.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

text: Zinn gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a011

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

speaker: a007
text: The three of you together hold more than he does — I need to know that number, not as a threat to him, but because if he decides we're a problem worth solving, I want us to already know what we can put together before he moves. Eron, Nessa, Zinn: tell me what you're each carrying, right now, in this room.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Eron.
